My role as the Architect is to design the target architecture on Google Cloud Run. I will create the core design decisions and component descriptions, storing them as memories. These memories will serve as the official design artifacts for other agents, like DevOps and the Synthesizer, to use.

First, I will define the mapping of AWS services to their GCP equivalents. This is a foundational decision record.

```json
{
  "tool": "brain_store_memory",
  "args": {
    "content": "## AWS to GCP Service Mapping Decision Record\n\n**Context:** As part of the migration of 100 microservices from AWS to Google Cloud, we need to map the currently used AWS services to their equivalent, cloud-native counterparts in GCP.\n\n**Decision:**\n\nThe following mapping will be used for the migration:\n\n| AWS Service | GCP Equivalent | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| EC2 (for microservices) | Google Cloud Run | Shift from IaaS to a fully managed serverless container platform to reduce operational overhead. |\n| Relational Database Service (RDS) | Google Cloud SQL | A fully managed relational database service that is compatible with the existing PostgreSQL databases. |\n| Simple Storage Service (S3) | Google Cloud Storage | Google's scalable and durable object storage solution, offering similar functionality to S3. |\n| Simple Queue Service (SQS) | Google Cloud Pub/Sub | A scalable, asynchronous messaging service that can effectively replace SQS for event-driven communication. |\n| Simple Notification Service (SNS) | Google Cloud Pub/Sub | Pub/Sub's fan-out capabilities make it a suitable replacement for SNS-style notification patterns. |\n| AWS IAM Roles | GCP IAM Roles & Service Accounts | GCP's IAM model provides granular control. We will use dedicated Service Accounts for each Cloud Run service. |\n",
    "category": "decision_record",
    "source": "mission-1769275135-architect",
    "tags": [
      "gcp",
      "aws",
      "migration",
      "architecture",
      "service-mapping"
    ]
  }
}
```
```json
{
  "tool": "brain_store_memory",
  "args": {
    "content": "## Containerization Strategy Decision Record\n\n**Context:** All microservices must be containerized for deployment to Google Cloud Run. We need a consistent and efficient strategy for creating container images.\n\n**Decision:**\n\n1.  **Primary Method: Multi-stage Dockerfiles.** Each microservice will have a dedicated, multi-stage `Dockerfile`. This approach provides maximum control and optimization, resulting in smaller, more secure production images by separating build-time dependencies from the final runtime environment.\n2.  **Secondary Method (for simple services): Google Cloud Buildpacks.** For microservices with standard language runtimes (e.g., simple Node.js or Python apps) and no complex system dependencies, Google Cloud Buildpacks may be used to simplify the build process. This will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.\n\n**Rationale:** Multi-stage Dockerfiles give us the fine-grained control needed for a diverse set of 100 microservices, ensuring performance and security. Buildpacks offer a faster, lower-effort alternative for less complex services, providing a good balance of efficiency and control.",
    "category": "decision_record",
    "source": "mission-1769275135-architect",
    "tags": [
      "gcp",
      "cloud-run",
      "containerization",
      "docker",
      "architecture"
    ]
  }
}
```
```json
{
  "tool": "brain_store_memory",
  "args": {
    "content": "## Target Networking Architecture Design\n\n**Context:** This document describes the networking design for the migrated microservices on Google Cloud. It serves as the specification for the architecture diagram and Terraform implementation.\n\n**Architecture Components:**\n\n1.  **Shared VPC:** A single Shared VPC named `vpc-prod-migration` will be created to host all shared networking resources. This centralizes network administration.\n2.  **Subnets:** The VPC will contain dedicated subnets for different components, such as `subnet-cloudrun-us-central1` and `subnet-cloudsql-us-central1`.\n3.  **Cloud SQL Instance:** A Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance will be deployed with a private IP address within the `subnet-cloudsql-us-central1` subnet.\n4.  **Serverless VPC Access Connector:** A Serverless VPC Access connector will be created and associated with the `subnet-cloudrun-us-central1` subnet. This is CRITICAL as it allows the serverless Cloud Run services to communicate with the Cloud SQL instance over the private network.\n5.  **Cloud Run Services:** All Cloud Run services will be configured to use the Serverless VPC Access connector for all outbound traffic. Ingress will be controlled via the `allow-internal-and-cloud-load-balancing` setting.\n6.  **Cloud NAT:** A Cloud NAT gateway will be configured for the `subnet-cloudrun-us-central1` to allow outbound internet access for services that need to call external APIs (e.g., payment gateways, 3rd party services). This provides a stable set of egress IP addresses.\n7.  **External HTTP(S) Load Balancer:** For public-facing services (e.g., an API gateway or user-facing frontend), an External HTTP(S) Load Balancer will be used. The backend for this load balancer will be a Serverless Network Endpoint Group (NEG) pointing to the relevant Cloud Run service(s).",
    "category": "architecture_design",
    "source": "mission-1769275135-architect",
    "tags": [
      "gcp",
      "cloud-run",
      "networking",
      "vpc",
      "architecture"
    ]
  }
}
```
```json
{
  "tool": "brain_store_memory",
  "args": {
    "content": "## Target IAM Strategy\n\n**Context:** A clear Identity and Access Management (IAM) strategy is required to ensure the principle of least privilege for all migrated services running on Google Cloud Run.\n\n**Strategy:**\n\n1.  **Dedicated Service Accounts:** Each microservice deployed on Cloud Run will be assigned its own dedicated GCP Service Account (SA). The naming convention will be `sa-<service-name>@<project-id>.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.\n2.  **Principle of Least Privilege:** Each SA will be granted only the minimum IAM roles required for its functionality.\n3.  **Example Role Bindings (based on sample services):**\n    *   **User-Auth Service (`sa-user-auth`):**\n        *   `roles/cloudsql.client`: To connect to the Cloud SQL database.\n        *   `roles/storage.objectAdmin`: To read and write user profile pictures in a dedicated Cloud Storage bucket.\n    *   **Order-Processing Service (`sa-order-processing`):**\n        *   `roles/cloudsql.client`: To connect to the Cloud SQL database.\n        *   `roles/pubsub.publisher`: To publish messages to Pub/Sub topics after processing an order.\n        *   `roles/pubsub.subscriber`: To pull messages from the incoming order queue subscription.\n    *   **Notifications Service (`sa-notifications`):**\n        *   `roles/pubsub.subscriber`: To receive events from various topics that trigger notifications.\n\n4.  **Cloud Build SA:** The default Cloud Build service account will be granted roles to push images to Artifact Registry (`roles/artifactregistry.writer`), deploy to Cloud Run (`roles/run.admin`), and act as a Service Account User (`roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`) for the microservice-specific SAs during deployment.",
    "category": "architecture_design",
    "source": "mission-1769275135-architect",
    "tags": [
      "gcp",
      "cloud-run",
      "iam",
      "security",
      "architecture"
    ]
  }
}
```
